chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who urinates and then forgets to wash his private part and performs wudu (ablution). He said: “He should wash his private part and not repeat his wudu (ablution).”
As for what Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who performs wudu (ablution) and forgets to wash his private part after having urinated, he said: “He should wash his private part and not repeat the salat (prayer).”

So this report is specific to one who did not find water, for in that situation, as we have mentioned, cleansing with stones sufficed him. Then if he finds water after that, he washes his private part, and repeating the salat (prayer) is not required of him. But if water was available, then that salat (prayer) does not suffice him, as we have explained and will clarify later, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer); the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: cleansing after relieving oneself; here, specifically with stones in the absence of water
key_terms.الْأَحْجَارِ: stones; used for istinja' when water is unavailable
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water; the means of purification whose availability affects the ruling
key_terms.ذَكَرَهُ: his private part; the organ to be cleansed after urination
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution); the ritual ablution for salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; here, washing the private part after urination

ai.seo_question: If someone urinates and forgets to wash himself before wudu, must he repeat his wudu or salat?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of one who urinates and forgets to wash the private part before performing wudu (ablution). The first report states that he should wash the private part without repeating wudu, while the second report is explained as applying to one who lacked water, in which case prior cleansing sufficed and the salat (prayer) need not be repeated.
